overview: The respawn packet is a state-reset command: the world reloads, so every anticheat that keeps per-player state must re-arm it on respawn. Simulation anticheats parse WrapperPlayServerRespawn on the send side and rebuild their player model (Grim, Shard, Artemis), while classic anticheats zero grace timers on PlayerRespawnEvent so freshly respawned players are not flagged by movement and combat checks. The packet itself is never flagged; it is the boundary that makes the checks after it trustworthy.

checks.name: PacketPlayerRespawn (Grim)
checks.purpose: Reset the entire simulated player model on respawn and dimension change: positions, ground flags, attributes, entity list and the death-screen state.
checks.how_it_works: The RESPAWN branch wraps the packet as WrapperPlayServerRespawn, invalidates the setback teleport (hasAcceptedSpawnTeleport = false), clears server entity positions on world change, and schedules a real-time task that resets onGround, pose, sprinting, food, known input, the self PacketEntity and the BadPacketsE/G/M/F state. KEEP_TRACKED_DATA and KEEP_ATTRIBUTES flags decide what survives on 1.20.2+; isWorldChange compares world name or dimension type to detect cross-dimension teleports that wipe chunks and entities.
checks.detects: Nothing directly. It prevents stale movement state (old ground flags, old velocity, old entity ids) from leaking across the respawn boundary, which would poison every downstream check.
checks.variations: Shard's handleRespawn clears compensatedEntities only; Artemis stamps lastRespawn in MiscellaneousPreProcessor and sets respawnTicks (150) in EmulatorPreProcessor; Kauri resets its lastRespawn TickTimer in PacketHandler; NCP re-inits moving data through dataOnJoin with the joinOrRespawn flag.

checks.name: Respawn pre-processing (Artemis)
checks.purpose: Stamp the respawn moment and clear inventory and vehicle state so every check can exempt the respawn window.
checks.how_it_works: fastHandle runs on the packet thread: GPacketPlayServerRespawn schedules a transaction-confirmed action that calls setLastRespawn(packet.getTimestamp()), closes the inventory state and drops the predicted vehicle. ExemptType.RESPAWN then exempts checks while lastRespawn is under three seconds or respawnTicks is positive, and MovementPreProcessor decrements respawnTicks each tick. The same timestamp is also set from the client's C16 PERFORM_RESPAWN command.
checks.detects: Nothing on its own; the mechanism is exemption bookkeeping. The dedicated DisablerRespawn check uses the respawn domain to catch clients that abuse the respawn window, while AimIdentical and BadPacketsN read respawnTicks to skip false positives.
checks.variations: Grim and Shard reset state on the packet directly; SalmonAC and FlopAC keep tick counters instead of wall-clock stamps; Kauri uses a TickTimer reset from WrapperPlayServerRespawn in its PacketHandler.

checks.name: Respawn-tick exemption (SalmonAC)
checks.purpose: Zero the per-player respawnTick on respawn so every movement and combat check skips the respawn window.
checks.how_it_works: PlayerEventListener.onRespawn (PlayerRespawnEvent) sets salmonPlayer.respawnTick = 0, and the counter increments in SalmonPlayer. Checks then bail early while the tick is under their threshold, from 20 ticks (ReachA, CriticalA, SpeedCode) to 60 ticks (TimerC, Invalid0A, JesusC). The same listener registers players on PlayerJoinEvent and zeroes respawnTick on join too.
checks.detects: Nothing directly: it is an exemption counter, and the corpus hits are the getRespawnTick() guards inside roughly 40 checks.
checks.variations: FlopAC guards with a respawnTimer.hasNotPassed(20) inside BadPacketsC, SpeedA/B and SprintA/B; LightAntiCheat keeps cache.lastRespawn in milliseconds and skips checks within 500 ms of respawn; ThotPatrol and Daedalus reset latency data on PlayerRespawnEvent.

checks.name: Respawn-window exemption (FlopAC)
checks.purpose: Skip the bad-packets teleport check while the player is still inside the respawn grace window.
checks.how_it_works: BadPacketsC watches the flying packet family and flags an invalid teleport when the client's horizontal delta exceeds the server-position speed. The exemption list includes getRespawnTimer().hasNotPassed(20), so a respawned player's first 20 ticks are never evaluated. The timer is armed from the respawn path in the action processor; the tinyprotocol WrappedOutRespawnPacket wrapper is the packet-side representation.
checks.detects: Nothing on its own; the guard prevents false flags for players that legitimately teleport into the world after respawn.
checks.variations: SalmonAC's respawnTick and LightAntiCheat's lastRespawn cache are the same grace-window idea; Grim instead resets the whole simulation and keeps checks active, trusting the reset rather than an exemption window.
